headline: Proof pack finalized
note: Finalized 2026-10-22 after the Round 4 close-out (verdict SOLID), on the final published binaries: hookcheck 0.1.16, actionpin 0.1.6, injectcheck 0.1.13, tracewatch 0.1.0. Every number below comes from the proof pack files (security-wave/proof/cloudflare-headtohead/). Track A (replaying the same corpora through Cloudflare's live service) was not run: it requires an Enterprise account with the AI Security add-on or a configured AI Gateway, which we do not have. No Cloudflare latency or accuracy figure is estimated anywhere.
source: Research brief: security-wave/overnight/inbox/cloudflare/compare-research.md (every claim cited to a Cloudflare page)

research_points.title: Cloudflare detects at runtime, through its edge
research_points.body: AI Security for Apps (formerly Firewall for AI) scores incoming requests to labeled LLM endpoints and exposes a prompt injection score from 1 to 99. The detection fields are an Enterprise-only paid add-on, enabled through their account team. Nothing in the product scans a repository or an issue before an agent reads it.

research_points.title: AI Gateway Guardrails adds about 500 ms per request, published
research_points.body: Guardrails sits between the app and the model provider and evaluates the assembled prompt at model call time, after the agent has already read the content. Cloudflare's own docs put the added latency at approximately 500 ms per request, more for long content, and responses are buffered (no streaming).

research_points.title: No per-request latency or injection accuracy is published for the WAF path
research_points.body: For AI Security for Apps, Cloudflare publishes a 2-second hard analysis cap and score bands, not a per-request latency figure and not a prompt-injection accuracy number. Any head-to-head latency or accuracy figure for that path would require an Enterprise account to measure; the proof pack says so instead of estimating.

research_points.title: No Cloudflare product scans repos or issue text at rest
research_points.body: Across the public docs reviewed (WAF, AI Gateway, Client-Side Security, Workers Builds), no self-serve Cloudflare product audits install hooks or agent config files in a repo, audits GitHub Actions pinning, or scans GitHub issue and PR text before an agent reads it. The one at-rest code offering is an invitation-only managed vulnerability service, not hook, pinning, or injection-in-issues coverage.
research_points.source: compare-research.md, absence scoped to the product docs reviewed

research_points.title: Their own incident advice is what these tools automate
research_points.body: For the September 2025 npm compromise, Cloudflare's post says Page Shield would have detected all 18 packages retrospectively (browser scripts; that surface never sees install-time execution) and saw no related activity among its users. Its remediation advice (audit dependencies, pin versions, scan repos for suspicious Actions changes) is published as manual steps. For Shai-Hulud and tj-actions, no Cloudflare detection claim or detection timeline is published.

our_measured.note: Our side, from the Round 4 close-out on the final binaries (named source per row). These are whole-estate scan times at rest, offline, on one shared VM; they are not per-request add-ons and are never tabulated against Cloudflare's per-request figures.

tracks: Track A (planned): the same labeled corpora replayed through both Cloudflare paths at pre-registered thresholds, if an account with the add-on is available; otherwise recorded as not measurable by us.
Track B: hook and persistence coverage. Cloudflare surface absent in docs; our coverage measured on the validation corpus.
Track C: Actions pinning coverage. Cloudflare surface absent in docs; our coverage measured on 176+ real repos.
